source.notes: Same driver as the Soave case, on SystemRKEos. The pair's KIJSRK equals its KIJPR (0.01289789), so azoth's kij lookup is not a source of error on this case.

derivation:
The driver was run with SystemRKEos at 330 K and 25 bar, methane 0.6 and n-butane 0.4, mixing rule 'classic'. It printed:

  beta 0.9525551759710986
  k    [6.18390905247986, 0.4173156446899031]
  x    [0.10104481348088883, 0.8989551865191111]
  y    [0.624851936790506, 0.3751480632094941]
  Zl   0.10944871595541934
  Zv   0.8556710632316012

azoth reproduces all six to 4.1e-12 on beta and at or better on the rest, the same residue the other cubic cases show and the same cause - both implementations stop on an rms change in ln K. The tolerance is 1e-10, well above the measured floor. RK differs from Soave only in the alpha term, `1/sqrt(Tr)` against Soave's fitted correlation, and the agreement confirms that that one difference is the whole difference.
